answer: Trust propagates through bounded random walks on the attestation graph, so influence decays with distance from an anchor rather than spreading without limit. A sybil cluster may resemble a karst cavity: dense internally, yet joined to honest nodes by a sparse cut. Its low conductance constrains walk escape and, together with min-cut transitivity bounds, limits aggregate voting weight; at the nadir, no internal sybil attestations alone can manufacture external trust.
